audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer names 'Yasuo Feral Scream' as the enemy ability to track - in the focus field, the cooldown breakdown, the loading tips, the enemyWin line and the dos. Feral Scream is Cho'Gath's own W. Separately, the content layer claims three times that Wind Wall eats your Rupture.
audit.why: Yasuo's kit is Way of the Wanderer, Steel Tempest, Wind Wall, Sweeping Blade and Last Breath. Wind Wall 'blocks all enemy projectiles', and Rupture is a ground-targeted zone cast at a location - Cho'Gath's kit carries no projectile flag on any ability. Telling a player their engage is blocked when it is not costs every fight they decline.
audit.corrected: Track Wind Wall (25/23/21/19/17s) and Sweeping Blade instead. Rupture goes through Wind Wall because it is not a projectile, and Feast is a 175-range melee execute the wall cannot touch either.
sources: champ-data/_kits/chogath.json (Q ground-targeted zone, no projectile flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 and level 6 were marked Skill and the two-item stage was given to Cho'Gath, while the page's own text says the lane turns 'in your favor by 4-5', calls 6 'your hardest kill threat', and says to 'give the late game to the scaler'.
audit.why: The chart disagreed with the prose at three stages, and the packet chart matches the prose.
audit.corrected: Skill / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Yasuo with ratings 5,6,6,6,7,6,3. EVEN 6/10 stands with a 52.84% win rate over 791 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes referenced 'his E cooldown' and 'the wind-wall' with no numbers.
audit.why: Sweeping Blade is 0.5 down to 0.1 seconds but cannot be re-cast on the same target for a few seconds, Steel Tempest is a flat 4 seconds and knocks up on its second stack, Wind Wall is 25 down to 17, and Last Breath is 70/50/30. The dash cooldown is irrelevant; the number of dashable bodies beside him is the real constraint.
audit.corrected: Count his dash targets rather than his cooldown, and commit when Wind Wall is on its 25 seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wind Wall's terrain property was never mentioned, and Steel Tempest's knockup was described only as 'crit poke'.
audit.why: Wind Wall is flagged terrain as well as blocksProjectiles, so it also cuts paths. Steel Tempest knocks up at two stacks, and that knockup is what sets up Last Breath.
audit.corrected: Named both in the don'ts and the cooldown list.

edits.before: Don't throw Rupture (Q) blind — Yasuo will E-dash sideways out of the delayed circle or just raise Windwall (W) and eat it for free. At level 1 it's even; he last-hits with ranged Steel Tempest while you farm and top off mana and HP off Carnivore. Once you hit 2 you have the real threat: bait his Windwall with a fake step-up or a single auto, and the moment it's down, land Q into Feral Scream (W) — the silence shuts off Steel Tempest and his E-dash, and the knockup-into-cone takes a huge chunk while he can't crit back.
edits.after: Don't throw Rupture blind - Yasuo simply Sweeping Blades sideways out of the circle. What he cannot do is wall it off: Wind Wall blocks projectiles, and Rupture is cast at a location, so the wall is irrelevant to your engage. At level 1 it is even; he last-hits with ranged Steel Tempest while you top off HP and mana on Carnivore. From 2 you have the real threat. Watch the minions beside him rather than his cooldown, because Sweeping Blade needs a body and cannot repeat on the same one - catch him with none and the knockup into Feral Scream lands with no answer at all.

edits.before: This is your window. Carnivore sustain and Vorpal Spikes (E) waveclear keep you healthy through his Steel Tempest poke, and every time his Windwall is on cooldown you can Q-W him for free since he has to burn his E-dash to dodge. At 6, Feast (R) is the kill button — point-blank true damage that ignores his MR, and Windwall can't block a melee execute. Watch his flow shield and his E cooldown; if he dashed through the wave to poke and has no minion left to dash to, he can't escape your combo for a few seconds — that's when you all-in.
edits.after: This is your window. Carnivore sustain and Vorpal Spikes waveclear keep you healthy through Steel Tempest poke, and the dash is the only thing that dodges your knockup - so track the bodies he can jump to, not the 0.5-second cooldown. At 6, Feast is the kill button: 175-range true damage that ignores his MR, and Wind Wall stops projectiles only, so it blocks neither the execute nor the Rupture that sets it up. If he has dashed through the wave to poke and has nothing left to jump to, that is your all-in.

notes: The whole full layer for this matchup had Cho'Gath's own Feral Scream pasted in as the Yasuo ability to track, so focus, loading, cooldowns, dos and enemyWin all pointed at the wrong champion's kit; worth grepping other matchups for the same substitution. I corrected the claim that Wind Wall blocks Rupture, which is clear from Riot's text on both sides. I did NOT correct the related claim that Wind Wall blocks your Vorpal Spikes line (wants.foe[0], early) - chogath.json carries no projectile flag on E, but 'needsResearch' is empty rather than negative, so I left that text alone and raised it as a question. Also: chogath.json tags Rupture with grounding, a tooltip-parse misfire on 'Ruptures the ground' (same on Malphite Q and Olaf Q), so I never claimed Rupture grounds Sweeping Blade.
